arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) successfully compromised a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via a malicious email attachment. The initial payload, 'chrome_helper.exe', executed through Outlook-launched PowerShell, deployed a ShadowPad variant using process hollowing and established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad IP and domain. Post-compromise activities included lateral movement attempts via SMB and Kerberos exploitation. The threat was detected via IDS signature for Cobalt Strike beaconing, though initial access went undetected by EDR and email security controls.

arguments.summary: A critical APT incident was detected originating from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42), attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon). The attack began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, leading to the execution of a ShadowPad variant via rundll32.exe from the Temp directory. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known malicious IP (198.51.100.23) and exhibited lateral movement behaviors, including SMB access to internal file servers and Kerberos TGT request attempts. Dynamic analysis confirmed malicious behavior and identified additional IOCs, including a second-stage payload and C2 domain. Despite detection, containment actions were denied due to policy and targeting validation issues.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_Loader {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory-resident Cobalt Strike beacons using common API patterns"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $a = "CryptEncrypt" wide ascii
        $b = "HttpSendRequest" wide ascii
        $c = "InternetConnect" wide ascii
        $d = { 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? 68 ?? ?? ?? ?? E8 ?? ?? ?? ?? 83 C4 14 } // Common stack-based API call pattern
    condition:
        all of ($a, $b, $c) or $d
}
